title: Taxonomic revision and phylogeny of the neotropical primary freshwater crabs of the genus Sylviocarcinus H. Milne Edwards, 1854 (Decapoda: Brachyura: Trichodactylidae) using morphological and molecular data
content:
Abstract
The neotropical freshwater crabs of the family Trichodactylidae have a wide distribution in South America. The use of integrated data, combining morphological and molecular analyses, has never been employed in the genus Sylviocarcinus H. Milne Edwards, 1854. We aimed to conduct a taxonomic revision and investigate the phylogenetic relationships of the five species within the genus. Preliminary species identification was undertaken through comparative morphological analysis of key taxonomic structures, while mitochondrial gene fragments (COI and 16S rRNA) deemed informative for evaluating relationships were used for phylogenetic reconstruction. Morphological variations were observed among the species, particularly in external carapace features, such as the structure/shape of the frontal margin, the male first gonopod (G1), and the fusion of pleonal somites. G1 proved to be the most informative primary structure for species differentiation. An identification key is presented. Congruence between morphological and genetic data was detected, with distinct phylogenetic lineages corresponding to groups determined by morphological characters. Molecular-based species delimitation analyses, however, revealed divergences with morphological data. Although delimitation methods indicate the existence of more species of Sylviocarcinus than the five currently formally recognized, morphological data indicated low intraspecific variation, which does not provide support for the description of new species.
